title: Emit metrics for end-to-end latency and tokens/sec (per-model) with cardinality guardrails
author: Omar El-Sayed
description: Summary: This PR adds first-pass metric emission for perf-canary runs: end-to-end latency histograms and tokens/sec (plus supporting counters) with per-model attribution. Metrics are emitted from the canary process (not the runtime) so we can alert even when runtime telemetry pipelines are delayed. Motivation: We need low-noise, per-model signals for p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput (tokens/sec) before we can wire dashboards/alerting. This also sets the label policy up front to avoid a repeat of past cardinality blowups (e.g., per-prompt identifiers or unconstrained model strings). Metrics added (Prometheus/OpenTelemetry bridge): perf_canary_request_e2e_latency_ms (histogram; attributes: model_id, model_version, region, tier, hardware_sku, outcome); perf_canary_request_tokens_per_second (histogram; computed from generated_tokens / decode_time; same attributes); perf_canary_generated_tokens_total (counter; same attributes); perf_canary_requests_total (counter; same attributes); perf_canary_metric_dropped_total (counter; attributes: metric_name, drop_reason) to make guardrail drops visible. Cardinality guardrails: model_id + model_version are sourced from control-plane config and validated against an allowlist at startup; we reject/replace unknown model identifiers with model_id="unknown" and increment perf_canary_metric_dropped_total (drop_reason=unknown_model). We also hard-cap unique label sets per process (default 500) to fail closed (drop + log) if someone accidentally adds a high-card dimension. Explicitly not emitted: prompt text, prompt hashes, request ids, customer ids, raw error strings. outcome is normalized to a small enum (ok | timeout | http_error | inference_error | cancelled). Notes: tokens/sec is computed as generated_tokens / max(decode_wall_ms, 1ms) and emitted only for successful runs; for failures we still emit latency + counters to avoid survivorship bias in alerting. Follow-ups: This PR does not include baseline comparison logic (see PR-19218) or region/SKU fanout config (PR-19226).
commits: metrics: add StatsEmitter for histograms/counters and structured label builder
canary: instrument request loop to record wall time + decode time + token counts
metrics: implement label cardinality guardrails (allowlist + unique series cap)
tests: add unit tests for label normalization and drop counters
docs: add metrics reference + example PromQL queries for p95 and tokens/sec
conversation: Logan Wright (review): Please confirm we’re not emitting any free-form strings (errors) as labels; we’ve been burned by this in the past. Also, do we have a way to know if we’re dropping metrics due to guardrails? Omar El-Sayed (author): Good call. outcome is now normalized to a small enum and we explicitly do not include error strings. Added perf_canary_metric_dropped_total with (metric_name, drop_reason) so drops show up on dashboards and can page us if it happens. Nadia Rahman (review): Model label source worries me: if someone configures model_id inconsistently (e.g., alias), we’ll fragment baselines. Can we enforce canonical ids? Omar El-Sayed (author): Updated to pull canonical model_id/model_version from the control-plane config schema; runner rejects values not in the validated canary target list. Anything else becomes model_id="unknown" and increments drop counter (we also warn once per minute to avoid log spam). Allison Grant (review): +1 on the series cap. What’s the default, and can it be overridden without code changes? Also please add a short metrics doc for Grafana/PromQL examples. Omar El-Sayed (author): Default is 500 unique label sets per process; override via PERF_CANARY_MAX_SERIES env var (documented). Added docs/metrics.md with example queries for p95 latency and tokens/sec. Noah Patel (review): tokens/sec computed from decode time only makes sense, but it can be noisy if decode_wall_ms is ~0 for short runs. Make sure you clamp/divide safely and only emit on success. Omar El-Sayed (author): Implemented clamp max(decode_wall_ms, 1ms) and only emit tokens/sec when outcome=ok. We still emit latency for all outcomes. Rina Kobayashi (review): Can we add a test that confirms prompt text never reaches metrics/log fields? Omar El-Sayed (author): Added a guard test around label builder; prompts never enter the metrics package. We also assert that request context does not pass prompt content to emitter APIs.
release_notes: perf-canary now emits per-model end-to-end latency histograms and tokens/sec metrics with strict label cardinality guardrails and drop counters for visibility.
